name: Texas Hold'em
description: Texas Hold'em is the world's most popular poker variant. Each player receives two private hole cards, and five community cards are dealt face-up on the table. Players make the best five-card poker hand using any combination of their hole cards and the community cards. The game features four rounds of betting and combines skill, strategy, and psychology.

content.text: Texas Hold'em is the world's most popular poker variant. Each player receives two private hole cards, and five community cards are dealt face-up on the table. Players make the best five-card poker hand using any combination of their hole cards and the community cards. The game features four rounds of betting and combines skill, strategy, and psychology.

Country/Region of Origin: Robstown, Texas, USA
Time Period: Early 1900s (circa 1920s)
Creator(s): Unknown (developed in Texas card rooms)
Etymology: Named after Texas, where it originated, and "Hold'em" refers to players holding their own cards while sharing community cards

Minimum Players: 2 (heads-up)
Maximum Players: 10 (full ring)
Optimal Players: 6-9
Partnerships: No (individual play)

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Standard 52-card deck
Poker chips for betting
Dealer button
Small blind and big blind markers
Table (preferably oval for 6-10 players)

Cards per Player: 2 (hole cards, face down)
Community Cards: 5 (dealt face up in stages)
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise, starting with small blind

items.text: Pineapple: Each player is dealt three hole cards and must discard one before the first round of betting. Otherwise same as Texas Hold'em.
Crazy Pineapple: Each player is dealt three hole cards and keeps all three until after the second betting round. Each active player must discard one card immediately before the turn is dealt.

Crazy Pineapple Hi-Lo 8 or Better: Crazy Pineapple with pot split between highest and lowest hands. Low hand: five different ranks 8 or lower, aces low, no straights or flushes. Best low is A-2-3-4-5.
Tahoe (Wichita Hold'em): Each player is dealt three hole cards and keeps all three until showdown. A player may use 0, 1 or 2 hole cards (not all three) with board cards to make their final hand.
Irish: Each player is dealt four hole cards, kept until after the second betting round. Before the turn, each active player must discard two cards, keeping two for turn and river.
Informal (No Burn): Home game variant: community cards dealt face down to the table at the start; three turned up after first betting round, one after second, one after third. No burn cards.
No Limit: Players may bet any amount up to their full stack at any time. Most common in tournaments and cash games.
Fixed Limit: Bet and raise amounts are fixed (e.g. small bet preflop and flop, big bet turn and river). Typically one bet plus three or four raises per round.
Pot Limit: Maximum bet or raise is the current pot size. Balances no-limit and fixed-limit play.
Heads-Up (2 Players): Two players only. Dealer posts small blind, non-dealer posts big blind. Action order and strategy differ from full table.
Short-Handed (3-5 Players): Played with three to five players. Tighter hand requirements than full ring; position and aggression matter more.
Full Ring (6-10 Players): Standard table size. Optimal with six to nine players. Tighter play than short-handed.
Straddle: Optional third blind (typically double the big blind) posted by the player to the left of the big blind before cards are dealt. Creates a larger pot and different action order.
Casino Versions: Formal card-room and casino rules: mandatory burn before each community deal, strict betting order, and house procedures.
